o: We need the absolute difference between the maximum salary in Engineering and the maximum salary in Marketing. Two scalar subqueries (one MAX per department) suffice; wrap them in ABS. From the sample: Engineering max = 102000, Marketing max = 53000, difference = 49000. The guarantee that both departments have rows means neither MAX returns NULL, so no COALESCE handling is needed.
k: MAX is computed per department via filtered subqueries; ABS handles the sign.

a.i: SELECT the absolute difference of two independent MAX aggregates, each restricted to its department with a WHERE clause.
a.t: O(rows) — two table scans for the MAX aggregates

a.i: Alternatively, aggregate the whole table once using CASE expressions inside MAX, then take the difference — a single scan pattern common in reporting queries.
s: MAX(CASE WHEN department='Engineering' THEN salary END) and likewise for Marketing in one SELECT.

w: Both forms are standard interview answers; conditional aggregation scales better when many departments are compared. Watch for NULL semantics if a department could be empty (problem guarantees it can't, but COALESCE(...,0) is a robust follow-up answer).
